Why is the address for a subverse preceded with a "/v/" and not just voat.com/askvoat?

I can't speak for the admins, but it's a sensible design. From a REST perspective it allows prefixes like /u/ for users, /v/ for subverses, and any other things that come up in the future. Having everything after voat.co be presumed to be a subverse would be a huge pain in the ass.

Pages with prefixes like /i/ or ending to .php are not rewrote to image folder. Am I going to get hurt with this set-up?

You're just shooting yourself in the foot a bit if you plan on utilizing the /u/ then you're better off utilizing /v/.

While you could remove the /v/, you're still going to need to pass in where you want to go which will look like voat.co/sub?askvoatat minimum. The ? generally denotes the parameter you're passing in and the sub denotes that you're looking for a subverse not a user. if you default to looking for a sub, and someone doesn't know that and tries to input a user, they are going to consistently run into problems and not understand why.

Generally you assume that your users are incapable of making deductive leaps, like the user needs a /u/ when subverses don't need a /v/. So what you're doing isn't necessarily wrong, it's just not best practice.

The software itself is completely free. You have to add the content yourself, which for me meant pulling movies and TV shows off of my DVD collection. I'm a huge fan of open source software and games that are free. There are tons of free software/games out there that get overlooked, minus the couple popular ones. I don't think many people realize that some of this software is actually really good, and there's a lot of it.

Games:
* osu! | Music/rhythm game with a huge community and online support
* Nitronic Rush | Pretty cool racing game
* OpenTTD | A transportation tycoon game
* IB | An excellent rpgmaker horror game
* itch.io | Tons of free games here

Software:
* Scupltris | Simple 3D modelling software for beginners
* Medibang paint pro | Comic creation and painting software
* Krita | A pretty awesome painting program
* Blender | 3D and animation suite
* LMMS | Digital audio workstation, like FL studio
* Godot | A gamecreation tool that can make 3d and 2d games
* GDevelop | Another game creation tool
* Polycode | Framework for making games / software
* y5writer | A tool helps with organizing everything when you write a book
